main_issue: Who will complete Agent D's unfinished pitch section after D's bereavement; resolved with D running the analysis from home and C prepping the data.

A-B.evidence: Both are sympathetic and say they'll sort it out (T3, T6), but B declines to help with the section (T12, T19) while A keeps organizing; no real conflict.

A-C.evidence: A asks C if C can do the analysis (T13) and C says no (T14); after A asks C to handle the data prep (T20), C agrees (T23).

A-D.evidence: A first says not to worry about work (T3, T9), D says the section is unfinished (T5); later A accepts D's offer to run the analysis ('Okay, if you're sure. Thank you', T18).

B-C.evidence: Both decline the analysis (T12, T14) and neither addresses the other; C later takes on the data prep (T23) while B keeps declining (T19).

B-D.evidence: B tells D 'We'll sort it out' (T6) while D says the section is unfinished; D's later plan (T15) and B's declining to help (T19) fit together without friction.

C-D.evidence: C asks what the data prep involves (T21), D explains (T22), C agrees (T23), and D thanks C (T24).
